result:
All the files check out. Here's the full trace from keystroke to rendered sidebar.

## Sign-in

The form lives in `src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx`, a client component (`LoginForm`) driven by `useActionState`. On submit it first runs client-side validation with `loginSchema.safeParse` (`src/schemas/auth.ts`), then invokes the Server Action `loginAction` in `src/actions/auth/login.ts` directly as the form's `action` — there's no fetch to an API route.

`loginAction` re-validates the same `loginSchema` server-side (never trust the client), calls `consumeRateLimit(ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID, "auth:login")`, and hands off to `login()` in `src/server/services/auth-service.ts`.

## Credential checking

`login()` does the real work: `userRepo.findUserByEmail(email)` and `userRepo.findPasswordHash(user.id)` (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`), then `verifyPassword(password, storedHash)` from `src/lib/hash.ts`. There's no bcrypt/argon2 dependency — it's a hand-rolled scrypt KDF over `node:crypto`, storing hashes as `scrypt:<saltHex>:<keyHex>` and comparing with `timingSafeEqual` for constant-time safety. A missing user and a wrong password both throw the identical "Those credentials did not match" to avoid user enumeration, and the rate limit is consumed *before* the check so brute-forcing is throttled regardless of outcome.

## Session creation

On success, `login()` calls `createSessionToken(userId)` in `src/server/services/session-service.ts`, which generates a 32-byte random token (`randomToken`), hashes it with SHA-256 (`hashToken`), and writes only the hash — plus `userId`, `activeOrgId`, `expiresAt` (30-day TTL) — into the `sessions` table via `sessionRepo.createSession()` (`src/server/db/schema/users.ts` / `src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts`). The raw token never touches the database. Back in `loginAction`, that raw token is set into the browser via `setSessionCookie(token, expiresAt)` in `src/lib/session.ts`:

```ts
jar.set(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, token, {
  httpOnly: true,
  sameSite: "lax",
  secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
  path: "/",
  expires: parseIso(expiresAt),
});
```

The cookie is named `taskflow_session`. So: the DB holds the token *hash* plus session metadata (userId, org, expiry); the browser holds only an opaque random string, no user id, role, or claims embedded in it.

## Re-establishing identity per request

`src/proxy.ts` (Next.js 16's renamed `middleware.ts`) does a cheap edge-level check: for any non-public path it just looks for the presence of the `taskflow_session` cookie and redirects to `/login?next=...` if it's missing — it explicitly cannot touch the database from the edge. The real verification happens server-side via `getSessionPrincipal()` in `src/lib/session.ts`, which reads the cookie, calls `resolveSession(token)` (hashes the token, looks it up in `sessions` joined to `users`), and returns a `SessionPrincipal` only if `expiresAt` is still in the future.

## "Still signed in" and expiry

Expiry is checked twice — once in the repository lookup (an expired row is treated as not found) and again explicitly in `getSessionPrincipal()`. There's no sliding/refresh; sessions just expire at the fixed 30-day mark, with a `purgeExpiredSessions` sweep for cleanup. The actual sign-in gate for the whole app is `src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`, which calls `getSessionPrincipal()` and `redirect("/login")` if null — the proxy's cookie-presence check is only a coarse first filter, not the source of truth.

## From bare identity to workspace authorization

Inside `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`, the principal is resolved again and passed, along with the `orgSlug`, into `resolveActorForOrg(principal, orgSlug)` (`src/server/services/session-service.ts`). That function loads the org by slug, looks up the caller's row in `members` via `memberRepo.findMember(org.id, userId)`, and — if the membership is active — builds an `Actor { userId, orgId, role }`. This `Actor` is the object every downstream authorization check operates on; if there's no active membership, the layout calls `notFound()`.

The layout renders `DashboardShell` (`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_components/dashboard-shell.tsx`), which passes `actor` down to `AppSidebar` (`src/components/domain/nav/app-sidebar.tsx`, a client component). The sidebar doesn't branch on `actor.role` directly; it calls `visibleNav(SIDEBAR_NAV, actor, flags)` from `src/config/nav.ts`, which filters a declarative nav tree by checking each item's permission `action` (e.g. `"member:invite"`, `"org:manage_billing"`) through `can(actor, action, resource)` in `src/lib/permissions.ts`. `can()` is the single authorization chokepoint: it enforces the cross-tenant guard (`actor.orgId === resource.orgId`), a platform-staff bypass, then a `ROLE_MATRIX` lookup ranked by `owner > admin > member > viewer`, plus ownership-based escalations. Whatever passes that filter is what actually renders as sidebar links — so the same declarative nav config, gated by the same `can()` function used everywhere else in the app, is what produces the "role-tailored" sidebar the user sees.
